You are an expert clinical documentation specialist familiar with Philippine healthcare standards. Your task is to process raw doctor's orders and summarize them for the "Course in the Ward" section of PhilHealth CF4.

RULES (FOLLOW THESE STRICTLY):
1. TENSE & VOICE (MANDATORY): Every sentence MUST be in past tense and passive voice. Change verbs: "start" -> "was started", "administer" -> "was administered", "obtain" -> "was obtained", "refer" -> "was referred", "consult" -> "was consulted". Do NOT use present tense ("is given", "are ordered") or imperative mood.
2. COMPLETENESS (MOST IMPORTANT): Include every clinically relevant detail from the orders: medications (dose, route, frequency), diagnostics, fluids, diet, oxygen and ventilator settings, labs, procedures, referrals, held or discontinued items, PRN conditions, monitoring, consult criteria. Orders continued from previous days are details too: name each with its dose in one sentence (e.g. "Drug A 500 mg IV q8h and Drug B 10 mg 1 tab OD were continued."), never just "medications were continued". Mention supplies and materials only when truly essential (e.g. a blood product or device used on the patient); otherwise just name the procedure they are for.
3. NO NAMES: Omit every physician and staff name, including signatures, initials, and names after slashes at the end of an order (e.g. "Dr. Cruz/ Santos/ JRL"); refer to the service instead (e.g. "IM-IDS", "Neurology", "Anesthesia", "the attending physician").
4. LENGTH & READABILITY: Keep it as short as possible without dropping any detail: no filler, no repeating an order, and the orders' own abbreviations (IV, q8h, PRN). Aim for about 5 sentences; when the orders need more, add sentences instead of lengthening them, and keep each sentence under about 35 words. Do not use bullet points or numbered lists.
5. CHRONOLOGICAL ORDER: The orders are numbered in the order they were written. Describe them in that sequence, combining only orders that are next to each other into one sentence. Do not add times or timestamps.
6. NO ADDITIONS: Do not add diagnoses, outcomes, or context not present in the orders. Copy drug names exactly as written; never add or substitute a generic or brand name.

The patient was referred to IM-Gastroenterology for joint management. ECG was requested for tachycardia, ABG and CXR for tachypnea and desaturation, and lipase, procalcitonin and creatinine for hypotension, while metoclopramide 10 mg IV was given for nausea. ALT, AST, ALP, total and direct bilirubin were requested for icteric sclera. For probable sepsis from intra-abdominal infection, PT/PA and blood CS x 2 sites were requested and antibiotics were shifted to piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g IV then q6h, to be renally adjusted. A 500 ml fast drip was given then regulated to 150 ml/hr, WAB CT scan with IV contrast was requested, and ICU admission was suggested. The patient was referred to IM-Cardiology, amylase, alk phos, Cl and Ca were added to the labs, and another 200 ml fast drip was given. The diet was shifted to NPO, TPN 1400 kcal was started to run for 36 hours, and the WAB CT scan was made STAT. IM-Cardiology added ALP, lipase, amylase, BUN, PT/PA and albumin, kept the patient on NPO with CBG q4h, and admitted the patient to the ICU. For metabolic acidosis, NaHCO3 160 mEq bolus was given, then a NaHCO3 drip of 160 mEq in 340 ml over 3 hours, with repeat ABG after 1 hour. A plain abdominal x-ray was requested, later revised to supine only. Calcium gluconate was given SIVP, then as a drip of 1 amp in 50 cc PNSS over 30 minutes q8h for 3 cycles. An NGT open to bedside bottle and an IFC were inserted, and urinalysis was sent. PLRS 1 L fast drip was given then regulated to 3 cc/kg/hr, SGOT, SGPT and fecalysis were requested, omeprazole 40 mg IV OD was planned, and paracetamol 600 mg IV q6h PRN for fever or pain was ordered. The patient was decked to the ICU with vital signs q15 minutes, IJ catheter insertion was suggested, and another 1 L PLRS fast drip was given. The patient was referred to IM-Pulmonology, Amphoter 40 mg IV was given then OD, and ABG was done immediately. PNSS 500 ml fast drip was given with PLRS at 120 ml/hr and ondansetron 4 mg IV. The patient was referred to TCVS for emergency ultrasound-guided triple-lumen IJ catheter insertion under local anesthesia at the ER-MOR, with written consent secured. NAC 1.2 g IV q12h was started, HsTrop I and CK-MB were requested during IJ catheter insertion, and stat WAB CT scan and bedside WAB ultrasound were requested. IM-Pulmonology requested chest ultrasound, targeted SpO2 of at least 90%, and placed HFNT or intubation on standby. The patient was referred to IM-Nephrology, and fecalysis with FOBT, HBsAg, anti-HBs, anti-HCV and anti-HAV IgM were requested. For AKI, furosemide 40 mg IV was given and consent was secured for triple-lumen IJ catheter insertion and hemodialysis. HD was ordered with a low-flux dialyzer for 3 hours, BFR 180-200, DFR 400, NSS flushing, UF 0 net and CBG q1h. WAB ultrasound focused on the pancreas, biliary duct and gallbladder fossa was requested and the CT scan was put on hold. An octreotide drip of 500 mcg in 95 cc PNSS was started with a 100 mcg bolus, then 10 cc/hr (50 mcg/hr). IVF was decreased to PNSS 1 L x 40 cc/hr and PLRS 1 L x 40 cc/hr, with the sodium bicarbonate drip at 167 cc/hr and TPN at 50 cc/hr. Once TPN was hooked, CBG was decreased to q6h, LRS was discontinued and PNSS decreased to 20 cc/hr, with the mainline to increase to 100 cc/hr once the bicarbonate was consumed. FBS and lipid profile were requested and piperacillin-tazobactam was adjusted to 2.25 g IV q6h with 0.75 g IV after every HD. Pantoprazole (Amphoter) 40 mg IV OD and NAC 1.2 g IV q12h were continued, calcium gluconate drips were held, and a CVP line was installed with a target CVP of 8-10 mmHg. Repeat ABG post-HD was requested and paracetamol was decreased to 300 mg IV q4-6h PRN for fever (T 37.8 C or higher). Bedside 2D echo after HD was requested and surgery was asked whether oral medications could be started. Albumin 1 vial was given over 1 hour during HD with UF set to 1 L net, PNSS was increased to 100 cc/hr, and repeat CBC and BUN were requested at 8 PM. IM-Pulmonology agreed with HD for a 150 cc left pleural effusion, LDH was added to the labs, and enoxaparin 0.6 SC OD was planned if there were no surgical plans. Serum K and creatinine were added, and adenosine 3 mg SIVP was given three times, each reassessed after 15 minutes (maximum 12 mg/day). A KCl drip of 40 mEq in 100 cc at 4 mEq/hr x 2 cycles was started, blood typing was added to the next extraction, and repeat CBC and BUN were requested in the AM.
